outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Fifty true or false facts, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: True or false: lightning never strikes the same place twice.
lines.a: False! The Empire State Building gets hit around twenty times a year.

lines.q: True or false: the Sun is a star.
lines.a: True! A pretty average one, too.

lines.q: True or false: spiders are insects.
lines.a: False! They're arachnids, with eight legs instead of six.

lines.q: True or false: botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
lines.a: True! It grows from the flower and carries the seeds.

lines.q: True or false: penguins live at the North Pole.
lines.a: False! Wild penguins live almost only in the southern hemisphere. Five down, nice and easy so far!

lines.q: True or false: bulls get angry at the colour red.
lines.a: False! Bulls can't really see red. It's the moving cape that sets them off.

lines.q: True or false: a whale is a mammal.
lines.a: True! Whales breathe air and feed their babies milk.

lines.q: True or false: bananas grow on trees.
lines.a: False! The banana plant is a giant herb, not a tree.

lines.q: True or false: water boils at a lower temperature on top of a mountain.
lines.a: True! Lower air pressure means it boils sooner.

lines.q: True or false: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level.
lines.a: True! Almost eight thousand eight hundred fifty metres.

lines.q: Round two, medium. True or false: ostriches bury their heads in the sand.
lines.a: False! They lower their heads to turn their eggs, which looks like it from far away.

lines.q: True or false: chameleons change colour mainly to hide.
lines.a: False! They mostly change colour to signal mood and control their temperature.

lines.q: True or false: Napoleon was unusually short.
lines.a: False! He was about average height for his time. Old French inches made him sound smaller.

lines.q: True or false: diamonds are made of carbon.
lines.a: True! The same element as the graphite in your pencil.

lines.q: True or false: koalas are bears.
lines.a: False! They're marsupials, with a pouch like kangaroos. Fifteen done, you're doing great!

lines.q: True or false: old window glass is slowly flowing like a liquid.
lines.a: False! Glass is a solid. Old panes were just made unevenly.

lines.q: True or false: cracking your knuckles causes arthritis.
lines.a: False! Studies have found no link. The pop is just gas bubbles.

lines.q: True or false: Mount Everest is still growing taller.
lines.a: True! A few millimetres a year as the plates keep pushing.

lines.q: True or false: the Eiffel Tower gets taller in summer.
lines.a: True! The iron expands in the heat, by up to about fifteen centimetres.

lines.q: True or false: Vikings wore horned helmets in battle.
lines.a: False! That idea mostly comes from nineteenth century costumes and opera.

lines.q: Round three, hard. True or false: in theory, Saturn could float in water.
lines.a: True! It is less dense than water, if you had a bathtub big enough.

lines.q: True or false: there are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
lines.a: True! About three trillion trees, and a few hundred billion stars.

lines.q: True or false: the Statue of Liberty was originally copper brown.
lines.a: True! It slowly turned green over about twenty years.

lines.q: True or false: your stomach gets a new inner lining every few days.
lines.a: True! Otherwise its own acid would wear it away.

lines.q: True or false: Einstein failed maths at school.
lines.a: False! He had mastered calculus by about fifteen. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: True or false: the Moon has quakes, just like Earth.
lines.a: True! Apollo astronauts left seismometers that recorded moonquakes.

lines.q: True or false: strawberries are true berries.
lines.a: False! Botanically they're not, but bananas and grapes are.

lines.q: True or false: a jiffy is a real unit of time.
lines.a: True! In electronics it can mean one sixtieth of a second.

lines.q: True or false: the Great Fire of London in sixteen sixty six killed thousands.
lines.a: False! Only six deaths were recorded, though the real number may be higher.

lines.q: True or false: chocolate is toxic to dogs.
lines.a: True! Dogs can't break down theobromine well. Thirty done, twenty to go!

lines.q: Round four, very hard. True or false: ketchup was once sold as medicine.
lines.a: True! In the eighteen thirties, as tomato pills for indigestion.

lines.q: True or false: the lighter was invented before the match.
lines.a: True! A hydrogen lighter came in eighteen twenty three, friction matches a few years later.

lines.q: True or false: Pluto has completed a full orbit of the Sun since it was discovered.
lines.a: False! It was found in nineteen thirty, and one orbit takes about two hundred forty eight years.

lines.q: True or false: bananas are slightly radioactive.
lines.a: True! A tiny bit, thanks to natural potassium. Totally harmless.

lines.q: True or false: a group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
lines.a: True! Best group name in nature.

lines.q: True or false: no bridge crosses the Amazon River.
lines.a: True! Its banks are soft and swampy, and few roads reach it.

lines.q: True or false: Hawaii moves a little closer to Japan every year.
lines.a: True! The Pacific plate carries it several centimetres a year.

lines.q: True or false: identical twins have identical fingerprints.
lines.a: False! Fingerprints form in the womb and are unique to each twin.

lines.q: True or false: the Sahara has always been a desert.
lines.a: False! Several thousand years ago it was green with lakes and grassland.

lines.q: True or false: cats can't taste sweetness.
lines.a: True! They lack a working sweet taste receptor. Forty done, legend round next!

lines.q: Legend round. True or false: Marie Antoinette said let them eat cake.
lines.a: False! There's no evidence she ever said it.

lines.q: True or false: the inventor of the Pringles can was buried in one.
lines.a: True! Fredric Baur's family put some of his ashes in a Pringles can in two thousand eight.

lines.q: True or false: France still used the guillotine when the first Star Wars movie came out.
lines.a: True! The last execution was in September nineteen seventy seven.

lines.q: True or false: Harvard University is older than calculus.
lines.a: True! Harvard opened in sixteen thirty six, decades before Newton and Leibniz.

lines.q: True or false: in the original novel, Frankenstein is the name of the monster.
lines.a: False! Victor Frankenstein is the scientist. The creature has no name.

lines.q: True or false: Columbus proved the Earth was round.
lines.a: False! Ancient Greeks had worked that out almost two thousand years earlier.

lines.q: True or false: a day on Mercury lasts longer than its year.
lines.a: True! Sunrise to sunrise takes about a hundred seventy six Earth days, a year only eighty eight. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: True or false: humans evolved from chimpanzees.
lines.a: False! We share a common ancestor that lived millions of years ago.

lines.q: True or false: Abraham Lincoln is in a wrestling hall of fame.
lines.a: True! He was a skilled wrestler as a young man and is honoured by the National Wrestling Hall of Fame.

lines.q: Final question. True or false: there are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
lines.a: True! Roughly ten to the one hundred twentieth games, against about ten to the eightieth atoms.
